from: Distinguish between the net cash flow of a month and the profit earned in that month.
to: In March a Windhoek furniture shop sells N$60 000 of goods, all on 60-day credit, and receives no other money. Its costs for the month, all paid in March, are N$45 000. Explain the difference between the shop's net cash flow for March and the profit it earned in March.
why: Distinguish is not used on the current AS papers; reworded to Explain at 3 marks - one difference, taken into a named business.

from: Distinguish between a month's opening balance and its net cash flow.
to: A Swakopmund bakery starts June with minus N$20 000 in the bank. During June its receipts are N$8 000 more than its payments. Explain the difference between the bakery's opening balance for June and its net cash flow for June.
why: Distinguish is not used on the current AS papers; reworded to Explain at 3 marks - one difference, taken into a named business.

from: A timber merchant with an agreed overdraft limit of N$40 000 forecasts closing balances of N$36 000 in April, N$52 000 in May, minus N$110 000 in June and minus N$108 000 in July. State what these figures tell the business.
to: A timber merchant with an agreed overdraft limit of N$40 000 forecasts closing balances of N$36 000 in April, N$52 000 in May, minus N$110 000 in June and minus N$108 000 in July. Explain what these figures mean for the business.
why: State is not used on the current AS papers; reworded to Explain at 3 marks and narrowed to one point - the June shortfall - applied to the merchant's figures.

from: Kavango Crafts is a partnership making furniture in Rundu. Its forecast shows closing balances of N$18 000, minus N$26 000, minus N$41 000 and minus N$58 000 over four months, against an overdraft limit of N$30 000. Sales are steady and profitable. Customers, mostly retailers, take 60 days to pay; the partnership pays its timber suppliers in 30 days and holds three months of timber in store. Recommend what the partners should do, and explain what each part of your recommendation does to the forecast.
to: Kavango Crafts is a partnership making furniture in Rundu. Its forecast shows closing balances of N$18 000, minus N$26 000, minus N$41 000 and minus N$58 000 over four months, against an overdraft limit of N$30 000. Sales are steady and profitable. Customers, mostly retailers, take 60 days to pay; the partnership pays its timber suppliers in 30 days and holds three months of timber in store. Evaluate the best way for the partners to improve the partnership's cash flow position.
why: Recommend is not used on the current AS papers; reworded to Evaluate at 12 marks (AO1 2, AO2 2, AO3 2, AO4 6), the shape of a paper's final part. The ordered recommendation the answer builds is the judgement Evaluate asks for.

from: A business lists the following for March: a credit sale of N$30 000 on 60-day terms, N$12 000 received from a customer who bought in January, wages of N$18 000 paid in March, and depreciation of N$4 000 on its delivery van. State which of these enter the March column of its cash flow forecast, and why.
to: A business lists the following for March: a credit sale of N$30 000 on 60-day terms, N$12 000 received from a customer who bought in January, wages of N$18 000 paid in March, and depreciation of N$4 000 on its delivery van. Identify which of these enter the March column of its cash flow forecast, and explain why.
why: State is not used on the current AS papers; reworded to Identify and Explain. Four items are asked for, so no single paper tariff is claimed.
A question with no command word does not model a paper question; reworded to Define at 2 marks.

from: A forecast's closing balance row reads N$36 000, N$52 000, N$11 000, N$4 000 for four consecutive months. What does that row tell the business?
to: A forecast's closing balance row reads N$36 000, N$52 000, N$11 000, N$4 000 for four consecutive months. Explain what that row tells the business.
why: A question with no command word does not model a paper question; reworded to Explain, and it asks for more than one paper part, so no single paper tariff is claimed.

from: Set out, in order, the steps for completing one month's column of a cash flow forecast.
to: Identify, in order, the steps for completing one month's column of a cash flow forecast.
why: Set out is not used on the current AS papers; reworded to Identify, in order. It asks for the whole sequence, which the papers ask for one point at a time, so it is kept as a recall card with no paper tariff.
